statusText: Tail risk is in the low band at 10% while Stress remains high at 74%. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold because the Globex session has now retraced in both directions: the up-leg to 30,920.75 was fully reversed and the rotation back to 30,779.50 has not extended. The demanding rate, energy and geopolitical backdrop is therefore expressed through Stress rather than Tail. The 13:00Z-15:00Z US cash-open window on 28 September remains the narrow flagged danger window for conditional opening-auction continuation risk.
headline: A second rotation inside a 141-point Globex range leaves NQ 0.32% below Friday's settle with Tail at 10%, while $93 WTI, a 5.18% 10-year and an unresolved Hormuz standoff hold Stress at 74%
body: Nasdaq-100 futures are near 30,790-30,802 in the Monday Globex session, down about 0.3% from Friday's 30,889.25 settlement, and the shape of that move is the central observation. Price opened the week higher to 30,920.75, was sold to 30,781.75, was bought back to the settlement area, and has now rotated down again to a marginal new low of 30,779.50. Yahoo Finance shows 30,790.25 at 01:16Z and Investing.com 30,801.50 on a slightly delayed quote, so both reads agree. The whole week so far therefore fits inside a 141-point band worth 0.46%, and every leg has been retraced, including the up-leg in full. That is two-way rotation, not the persistent one-way path Tail measures, which is why Tail stays in the low band at 10% despite price sitting near the bottom of the range. S&P 500 futures at 7,784.00 are 0.25% lower inside a 7,779-7,803 band, an aligned move with no index-specific dislocation, and Asian cash is mixed rather than risk-off, with the Nikkei up 0.29%, the Topix up 0.17%, the Kospi down 0.41% after a two-day holiday and the ASX 200 flat. The backdrop remains demanding, and it is carried by Stress. WTI crude is $93.12, up 0.77% inside a $92.69-$93.60 range, having eased back from the $93.55 level Reuters reported at 22:02Z on the reopen; Brent is above $106. The driver is unresolved rather than escalating: President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on 27 September that Tehran had not yet received an official response through mediators and would decide once it did. That is a live geopolitical discontinuity risk and the principal Stress anchor, but an oil complex now retracing its reopen spike is not evidence of a pathological equity path. Rates are the second anchor. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for 24 September shows the 2-year at 4.87%, the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47%, after the 10-year reached a 19-year high reported near 5.22% on Friday and the FOMC raised its target range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September. Cash equities still closed the week higher and the VIX settled Friday at 14.87, down 5.11%, though no live volatility read exists in the weekend gap. The shared context collector is of limited use this hour: its futures and calendar sections are unavailable, and at roughly 92 minutes old its payload has just passed the 90-minute freshness threshold, so its latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections are treated only as delayed Friday background. That background is constructive but widely dispersed, with Microsoft up 3.66% and Qualcomm up 3.97% against Meta down 3.33% and Intel down 3.45%, which is supporting colour for two-way rotation rather than evidence of current NQ structure. Tail therefore holds at 10% in the low band, Stress eases one point to 74% as the energy impulse decays, and Confidence is held at 77% on two independent futures reads, fresh Asian cash levels, authoritative H.15 yields and verified weekend reporting, offset by the absent live volatility and cash-yield reads.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours are covered by published Claude assessments and none has been revised. Tail stayed inside the 6%-14% low band throughout, drifting up from 6% across the quiet weekend to a 14% peak at the Sunday futures reopen before falling back to 9% once the reopen round trip completed. Stress climbed steadily from 54% to 76% as the long-end yield and oil backdrop was reassessed through the non-trading window, and eased marginally at the end. Confidence fell from 73% to 67% in the thinnest overnight hours, recovered to 79% as fresh weekend reporting arrived, and settled near 77%. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green with a normal dominant mode.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 01:00Z hour on 28 September through 00:00Z on 29 September. Tail is held in the low band for 22 of the 24 hours and lifts to the 20% watch band only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z US cash-open hours, where unobserved opening-auction continuation is the specific structure of concern and the dominant mode is modelled as mixed. Stress stays in the high band throughout on generational long-end yields, a $93 oil complex, a hiking Fed and the unresolved Hormuz standoff, easing to 71% only at the end of the horizon. Confidence dips through the remaining thin Asian hours and improves as European and then US price discovery arrives, peaking at 79% before the cash open. Monday's scheduled catalysts are limited to the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index and a Barkin speech; the week's high-impact releases, including Core PCE, ISM Manufacturing and Non-Farm Payrolls, fall after this horizon and are held in the events calendar.
